selected_mechanism.name: NSF Regional Innovation Engine — Alaska Critical Minerals Accelerator (AI mineral-discovery cooperative agreement)

news_trigger.what_happened: The new Critical Minerals Accelerator Engine in Alaska will receive $15 million in funding for two years and up to $160 million over 10 years. The organization will be located at and led by UAF's Geophysical Institute.

selected_mechanism.one_line_definition: An NSF Regional Innovation Engine cooperative agreement that funds a UAF-led coalition to use artificial intelligence to locate and commercialize Alaska critical-mineral deposits, structured as a $15M two-year seed with an NSF-controlled option to scale to ~$160M over a decade.

layers.name: NSF award authority / source-selection
layers.what_it_does: Selects and funds the Engine as one of a new cohort of Regional Innovation Engines; establishes the $15M/two-year seed award.
layers.controlling_actor: NSF Directorate for Technology, Innovation and Partnerships (TIP)

layers.name: Continuation / milestone tranche gate
layers.what_it_does: Converts the seed award into the ~$160M decade tranche only on demonstrated milestone progress; as a cooperative agreement NSF retains unilateral continue/decline authority tranche-by-tranche.

layers.name: Lead institution / Engine CEO (AI method owner)
layers.what_it_does: Hosts and operates the Engine; directs the AI-driven mineral-discovery and biological-extraction research program.
layers.controlling_actor: UAF Geophysical Institute (host) with Lee Ann Munk as Engine CEO and UAF geosciences professor

layers.name: Land / subsurface-estate partner
layers.what_it_does: Controls access to the ground the AI targets; ANCSA subsurface estate holder whose consent gates whether AI-identified deposits can be explored or developed.
layers.controlling_actor: NANA Regional Corporation, Lance Miller, VP Natural Resources; Alaska Silver as industry exploration partner

chokepoint.binary_decision: At the year-two milestone review (~2028), NSF unilaterally decides continue-or-decline on the ~$160M scaling tranche. Because the Engine is a cooperative agreement (not a grant), it is a single funder's go/no-go, not a shared committee veto. Secondary asymmetric chokepoint: NANA Regional Corporation (Lance Miller, VP Natural Resources) independently controls subsurface-estate access to the deposits the AI targets.

selected_mechanism.ak_consequence: Critical-minerals mining. Whether Alaska's AI-driven mineral-discovery engine scales past its $15M seed depends on NSF's TIP Directorate year-two milestone/continuation decision (~2028) and NANA Regional Corp's subsurface-estate access, which together gate whether AI exploration reaches Northwest Alaska deposits this decade. Alaska holds 56 of 60 USGS-designated critical minerals.
selected_mechanism.structural_read: NSF Engines are cooperative agreements, not grants. The $160M over 10 years headline is optionality, not committed capital, and NSF's TIP Directorate can decline continuation at the milestone review within its own authority. The load-bearing machinery is a two-key structure, a federal funder (TIP) holding the money go/no-go and a private ANCSA landowner (NANA) holding the ground go/no-go, with AI as the intrinsic method that only produces value if both keys turn. AI here is not a bolt-on, it is the Engine's core commercialization thesis (using AI to locate deposits and biological methods to extract them), which is why the mechanism qualifies for The Stack even though the news brief itself omits the word AI.
selected_mechanism.forward_implication: A program manager or allocator with Alaska critical-minerals exposure (Alaska Silver, NANA-linked JVs, exploration vendors) should this week map their acreage against the Engine's declared target regions and NANA's subsurface estate, and calendar the NSF TIP year-two milestone/continuation review as the single binary that gates the ~$160M decade tranche, treating the $160M as an option, not a commitment.
